# Question and experimental design

Did weed biomass differ among five soybean management systems, and did system
responses vary among site-years? Total weed biomass is the primary outcome.
Inter-row weed biomass is a secondary modeled outcome, while in-row biomass is
reported descriptively because exploratory inferential models were unstable or
showed residual problems.

The experiment included three site-years and four blocks per site-year. Cereal
rye termination was assigned to whole plots within blocks: roller-crimped
(rolled) or moldboard-plowed (tilled). Within rolled whole plots, management
subplots received no supplemental weed control (RNO), inter-row mowing (RIM),
or high-residue cultivation (RIC). Within tilled whole plots, subplots received
mowing (TIM) or cultivation (TIC). Thus, the five systems are not a fully
crossed factorial. Comparisons involving different termination methods require
whole-plot replication; comparisons within a termination method use subplot
replication.

Field records should be checked for the documented 2023 treatment implementation
error and incomplete RIC cultivation schedule before manuscript reporting.
Treatment labels here follow randomized assignments.

# Analysis plan

Total weed biomass is the primary response. We fit a split-plot Tweedie GLMM
with site-year-specific dispersion and report planned within-site-year contrasts.
Inter-row weed biomass is analyzed separately with a full treatment × site-year
Tweedie GLMM. In-row biomass is summarized descriptively; exploratory models
were examined but are not used for inference. Finally, an observed stacked
in-row/inter-row figure presents total biomass with arithmetic SE bars and
model-derived compact-letter displays (CLDs) for total and inter-row weed biomass.
These CLDs summarize unadjusted model-based pairwise Wald tests within each
site-year (an unprotected Fisher LSD-style procedure), separately from the
Holm-adjusted planned contrasts. They are exploratory rather than
familywise-error-controlled inference.

All zone biomass values are expressed per hectare of the **entire 0.5 m²
quadrat**, so in-row and inter-row components sum to total weed biomass.

# Setup

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = TRUE, warning = TRUE, error = FALSE)
```

```{r packages-and-settings, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(conflicted)
library(glmmTMB)
library(DHARMa)
library(emmeans)
library(WrensBookshelf)

conflicts_prefer(dplyr::filter)
conflicts_prefer(dplyr::select)

method_levels <- c("Roller-crimper", "Moldboard plow")
treatment_levels <- c("RNO", "RIM", "RIC", "TIM", "TIC")
treatment_labels <- c(
  RNO = "Rolled,\nno control",
  RIM = "Rolled,\nmowing",
  RIC = "Rolled,\nhigh-residue cultivation",
  TIM = "Tilled,\nmowing",
  TIC = "Tilled,\ncultivation"
)
experiment_labels <- c(
  V_2023 = "2023 – Field V",
  O2E_2024 = "2024 – Field O2 East",
  O2W_2024 = "2024 – Field O2 West"
)
method_lookup <- c(
  RNO = "Roller-crimper", RIM = "Roller-crimper",
  RIC = "Roller-crimper", TIM = "Moldboard plow", TIC = "Moldboard plow"
)
treatment_colors <- setNames(
  WrensBookshelf::WB_brewer(name = "WhatWellBuild", n = 5, type = "discrete"),
  treatment_levels
)
theme_set(theme_classic(base_size = 16))
show_table <- function(x, caption, digits = 1) {
  knitr::kable(x, caption = caption, digits = digits)
}
```

# Import and validate

The processed data are assumed already converted to kg/ha. Do not convert
these quantities again. Check the source and units against `data_prep.Rmd`.

```{r import-and-check, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
processed_file <- here("data", "processed", "combined_processed.rds")
processed_data <- readRDS(processed_file)

show_table(
  tibble(input = "data/processed/combined_processed.rds",
         MD5 = unname(tools::md5sum(processed_file))),
  "Processed-data provenance"
)

responses <- c(
  "weed_biomass_kg_ha",
  "inrow_weed_biomass_kg_ha",
  "interrow_weed_biomass_kg_ha"
)
required <- c("site_year", "block", "treatment", responses)
missing_columns <- setdiff(required, names(processed_data))
if (length(missing_columns)) {
  stop("Missing processed-data columns: ", paste(missing_columns, collapse = ", "),
       ". Confirm the names and units in data_prep.Rmd before proceeding.")
}

weed_data <- processed_data |>
  select(all_of(required)) |>
  mutate(across(c(site_year, block, treatment), as.character))

if (anyNA(weed_data[c("site_year", "block", "treatment")]) ||
    any(vapply(weed_data[c("site_year", "block", "treatment")],
               function(x) any(trimws(x) == ""), logical(1)))) {
  stop("Missing or blank experimental identifiers.")
}
if (!setequal(unique(weed_data$site_year), names(experiment_labels))) {
  stop("Site-year codes do not match experiment_labels.")
}
if (!setequal(unique(weed_data$treatment), treatment_levels)) {
  stop("Treatment codes do not match treatment_levels.")
}
for (response in responses) {
  y <- weed_data[[response]]
  if (!is.numeric(y) || anyNA(y) || any(!is.finite(y)) || any(y < 0)) {
    stop(response, " must contain finite, nonnegative values without missing data.")
  }
}

plot_counts <- weed_data |> count(site_year, block, treatment)
block_counts <- plot_counts |> count(site_year, block, name = "n_treatments")
experiment_counts <- block_counts |> count(site_year, name = "n_blocks")
if (any(plot_counts$n != 1L) || any(block_counts$n_treatments != 5L) ||
    any(experiment_counts$n_blocks != 4L)) {
  stop("Expected one subplot per treatment and four blocks in each site-year.")
}

weed_data <- weed_data |>
  mutate(
    site_year = factor(site_year, levels = names(experiment_labels)),
    treatment = factor(treatment, levels = treatment_levels),
    primary_method = factor(
      unname(method_lookup[as.character(treatment)]), levels = method_levels
    ),
    block_id = interaction(site_year, block, drop = TRUE),
    whole_plot_id = interaction(block_id, primary_method, drop = TRUE)
  )

show_table(
  weed_data |>
    group_by(site_year) |>
    summarise(
      n_plots = n(), n_blocks = n_distinct(block_id),
      n_whole_plots = n_distinct(whole_plot_id),
      zero_total = sum(weed_biomass_kg_ha == 0),
      .groups = "drop"
    ),
  "Validated weed biomass observations"
)
```

```{r validate-zone-sum}
# The two zone components must sum to total biomass on the same area basis.
zone_discrepancy <- with(
  weed_data,
  weed_biomass_kg_ha - inrow_weed_biomass_kg_ha - interrow_weed_biomass_kg_ha
)
stopifnot(max(abs(zone_discrepancy)) < 1e-5)
```

# Total weed biomass

## Observed summaries

```{r observed-total-summary, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
total_summary <- weed_data |>
  group_by(site_year, treatment) |>
  summarise(
    n_plots = n(),
    n_zeros = sum(weed_biomass_kg_ha == 0),
    mean_biomass = mean(weed_biomass_kg_ha),
    sd_biomass = sd(weed_biomass_kg_ha),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
show_table(total_summary, "Observed total weed biomass (kg/ha)")
```

## Primary Tweedie model

The model retains block and termination whole-plot intercepts for the split-plot
design, even if estimated variance components approach zero. A near-zero
estimate is a boundary estimate, not proof that whole-plot uncertainty is
negligible; including random intercepts does not by itself calibrate
asymptotic tests for four blocks per site-year. Sum contrasts
support joint Type III tests. The site-year dispersion model is retained after
the initial common-dispersion model showed heterogeneous dispersion.

```{r total-weed-models, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
contrasts(weed_data$treatment) <- contr.sum(5)
contrasts(weed_data$site_year) <- contr.sum(3)

total_weed_model_full <- glmmTMB(
  weed_biomass_kg_ha ~ treatment * site_year +
    (1 | block_id) + (1 | whole_plot_id),
  family = tweedie(link = "log"),
  data = weed_data
)

weed_model_disp <- glmmTMB(
  weed_biomass_kg_ha ~ treatment * site_year +
    (1 | block_id) + (1 | whole_plot_id),
  dispformula = ~ site_year,
  family = tweedie(link = "log"),
  data = weed_data
)

show_table(
  as.data.frame(AIC(total_weed_model_full, weed_model_disp)) |>
    tibble::rownames_to_column("model"),
  "Comparison of Tweedie dispersion specifications", digits = 2
)
anova(total_weed_model_full, weed_model_disp)
```

## Model diagnostics

Simulation-based checks and convergence are reported for the retained model.
With only four blocks per site-year, asymptotic Wald tests (df = Inf) and
particularly borderline comparisons across termination systems warrant caution.
Estimated variance components near zero are reported, not interpreted as
proof of negligible whole-plot uncertainty.

```{r total-weed-model-checks, fig.width=9, fig.height=5.5}
stopifnot(weed_model_disp$fit$convergence == 0L)
stopifnot(isTRUE(weed_model_disp$sdr$pdHess))
cat("Optimizer message:", weed_model_disp$fit$message, "\n")
print(VarCorr(weed_model_disp))
print(glmmTMB::family_params(weed_model_disp))

set.seed(123)
total_weed_resid <- DHARMa::simulateResiduals(weed_model_disp, n = 1000)
plot(total_weed_resid)
DHARMa::testDispersion(total_weed_resid)
DHARMa::testZeroInflation(total_weed_resid)
DHARMa::testUniformity(total_weed_resid)
DHARMa::plotResiduals(total_weed_resid, form = weed_data$site_year)
```

## Management effects and planned contrasts

Six selected comparisons are adjusted using Holm **within each site-year**.
The unadjusted model-based pairwise Wald tests used for figure letters
(Fisher LSD-style, without an omnibus protection step) are distinct from
Holm-adjusted planned contrasts.
The letters are descriptive summaries of model-based pairwise tests, not proof
that treatments sharing a letter are equivalent.

```{r total-weed-effects, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
car::Anova(weed_model_disp, type = 3, component = "cond")

total_weed_emm <- emmeans::emmeans(
  weed_model_disp, ~ treatment | site_year, component = "cond"
)
show_table(
  as.data.frame(summary(total_weed_emm, type = "response")),
  "Estimated total weed biomass by management system and site-year", digits = 2
)

stopifnot(identical(levels(weed_data$treatment), treatment_levels))
planned_contrast_weights <- list(
  "RIM vs TIM" = c(0, 1, 0, -1, 0),
  "RIC vs TIC" = c(0, 0, 1, 0, -1),
  "RIM vs RIC" = c(0, 1, -1, 0, 0),
  "RNO vs RIM" = c(1, -1, 0, 0, 0),
  "RNO vs RIC" = c(1, 0, -1, 0, 0),
  "RIM vs TIC" = c(0, 1, 0, 0, -1)
)
total_weed_contrasts <- emmeans::contrast(
  total_weed_emm, method = planned_contrast_weights, by = "site_year"
)
show_table(
  as.data.frame(summary(total_weed_contrasts, type = "response",
                        infer = c(TRUE, TRUE), adjust = "holm")),
  "Planned biomass ratios: Holm-adjusted p-values, Bonferroni-adjusted confidence intervals (within site-year)", digits = 3
)
```

## Whole-plot sensitivity checks

These checks are exploratory sensitivity analyses, not replacement inferential
models. The 2^4 sign enumeration has a smallest attainable two-sided p-value
of 0.125 with four pairs. Treat it as a sign-flip sensitivity check: an exact
randomization-test interpretation would require confirming that independent
within-block flips correspond to allowable assignments under the two-stage
randomization. Otherwise, validity rests on a symmetry/exchangeability
assumption for paired differences, which is not established here.

```{r total-weed-block-sensitivity, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
weed_wide <- weed_data |>
  select(site_year, block_id, treatment, weed_biomass_kg_ha) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = treatment,
                     values_from = weed_biomass_kg_ha)
stopifnot(nrow(weed_wide) == 12L, !anyNA(weed_wide[treatment_levels]))

planned_pairs <- tibble::tribble(
  ~contrast, ~a, ~b,
  "RIM vs TIM", "RIM", "TIM",
  "RIC vs TIC", "RIC", "TIC",
  "RIM vs RIC", "RIM", "RIC",
  "RNO vs RIM", "RNO", "RIM",
  "RNO vs RIC", "RNO", "RIC",
  "RIM vs TIC", "RIM", "TIC"
)

paired_results <- purrr::pmap_dfr(planned_pairs, function(contrast, a, b) {
  weed_wide |>
    mutate(difference = .data[[a]] - .data[[b]]) |>
    group_by(site_year) |>
    group_modify(~ {
      result <- stats::t.test(.x$difference)
      tibble::tibble(
        n_blocks = nrow(.x),
        mean_difference = mean(.x$difference),
        ci_lower = result$conf.int[1],
        ci_upper = result$conf.int[2],
        p_value_unadjusted = result$p.value
      )
    }) |>
    ungroup() |>
    mutate(contrast = contrast, .before = 1)
})
show_table(paired_results,
           "Block-paired sensitivity (kg/ha; unadjusted paired t-tests)", digits = 3)
```

```{r total-weed-sign-flip, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# All 2^4 possible sign assignments for four block pairs
sign_matrix <- as.matrix(expand.grid(rep(list(c(-1, 1)), 4)))

sign_flip <- function(d) {
  stopifnot(length(d) == 4L, all(is.finite(d)))
  possible <- as.vector(sign_matrix %*% d / 4)
  tibble::tibble(
    n_blocks = 4L,
    n_negative = sum(d < 0),
    mean_difference = mean(d),
    sign_flip_p_two_sided = mean(abs(possible) >= abs(mean(d)) - 1e-10)
  )
}

randomization_results <- purrr::map_dfr(
  split(weed_wide, weed_wide$site_year), function(dat) {
    purrr::map_dfr(c("RIM vs TIM", "RIC vs TIC"), function(label) {
      pair <- planned_pairs |> filter(contrast == label)
      sign_flip(dat[[pair$a]] - dat[[pair$b]]) |>
        mutate(site_year = as.character(dat$site_year[1]),
               contrast = label, .before = 1)
    })
  }
)
show_table(randomization_results,
           "Exploratory whole-plot sign-flip sensitivity", digits = 3)
```

## Split-plot Tweedie model and diagnostics

The full treatment × site-year model converged in the exploratory analysis;
no treatment × site-year cell consisted entirely of zeros. Its dispersion was
adequately represented by the common-dispersion specification.

```{r interrow-weed-model, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Initial Tweedie model for inter-row weed biomass

library(glmmTMB)

# Fit the full treatment × site-year model
interrow_weed_model_full <- glmmTMB(
  interrow_weed_biomass_kg_ha ~
    treatment * site_year +
    (1 | block_id) +
    (1 | whole_plot_id),
  family = tweedie(link = "log"),
  data = weed_data
)

# Model summary
summary(interrow_weed_model_full)

# Convergence checks (fail early if the retained model is not regular)
stopifnot(interrow_weed_model_full$fit$convergence == 0L)
stopifnot(isTRUE(interrow_weed_model_full$sdr$pdHess))
cat("Optimizer message:", interrow_weed_model_full$fit$message, "\n")

# Random-effect variance estimates
VarCorr(interrow_weed_model_full)

# Tweedie power parameter
glmmTMB::family_params(interrow_weed_model_full)
```

```{r interrow-weed-diagnostics, fig.width=9, fig.height=5.5}
# Residual diagnostics for inter-row weed biomass

set.seed(123)

interrow_sim_full <- DHARMa::simulateResiduals(
  fittedModel = interrow_weed_model_full,
  n = 1000
)

# Standard DHARMa diagnostic plots
plot(interrow_sim_full)

# Formal diagnostic tests
DHARMa::testDispersion(interrow_sim_full)
DHARMa::testZeroInflation(interrow_sim_full)
DHARMa::testUniformity(interrow_sim_full)

# Residuals grouped by site-year
DHARMa::plotResiduals(
  interrow_sim_full,
  form = weed_data$site_year
)
```

## Joint tests, estimates, and contrasts

Seven selected contrasts are assessed within each site-year with Holm-adjusted
p-values. Their displayed confidence intervals are Bonferroni-adjusted, not
Holm-adjusted. TIM vs TIC was added after inspecting the results and should be
identified as exploratory in reporting. Wald-based tests are asymptotic and
warrant caution with four blocks per site-year.

```{r interrow-weed-fixed-effects, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Fixed-effect tests for inter-row weed biomass

car::Anova(
  interrow_weed_model_full,
  type = 3,
  component = "cond"
)

# Estimated marginal means within each site-year
interrow_weed_emm <- emmeans::emmeans(
  interrow_weed_model_full,
  ~ treatment | site_year,
  component = "cond"
)

# Back-transformed estimates and confidence intervals
summary(
  interrow_weed_emm,
  type = "response"
)
```

```{r interrow-weed-final-contrasts, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Seven management-system contrasts within each site-year

# Reuse interrow_weed_emm calculated above.

interrow_contrasts <- emmeans::contrast(
  interrow_weed_emm,
  method = list(
    "RIM vs TIM" = c(0, 1, 0, -1, 0),
    "RIC vs TIC" = c(0, 0, 1, 0, -1),
    "RIM vs RIC" = c(0, 1, -1, 0, 0),
    "RNO vs RIM" = c(1, -1, 0, 0, 0),
    "RNO vs RIC" = c(1, 0, -1, 0, 0),
    "RIM vs TIC" = c(0, 1, 0, 0, -1),
    "TIM vs TIC" = c(0, 0, 0, 1, -1)
  ),
  by = "site_year"
)

# Ratios, confidence intervals, and adjusted p-values
summary(
  interrow_contrasts,
  type = "response",
  adjust = "holm",
  infer = c(TRUE, TRUE)
)
```

## Inter-row post hoc groupings and model-estimated figure

For figure annotations, unadjusted model-based pairwise Wald comparisons
(Fisher LSD-style) are implemented using `adjust = "none"` for treatment
means **within each site-year**. These are *unprotected* LSD-style tests, not a
protected Fisher LSD procedure gated by a significant site-year-specific omnibus
F test. They do not control the familywise error rate across all pairs; report
this limitation and prioritize the preselected, Holm-adjusted contrasts for
confirmatory interpretation. Lowercase CLD letters correspond to inter-row
biomass only, with **a** assigned to the highest estimated group. Shared
letters indicate no detected difference, not equivalence.

The bars and error bars show response-scale model estimates ± SE and are
separate from the observed stacked figure below.

```{r interrow-weed-final-figure, fig.width=11, fig.height=6, out.width="100%", message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(emmeans)

# Model-estimated means and SE on the response scale
interrow_fig_data <- summary(
  interrow_weed_emm,
  type = "response"
) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  mutate(
    treatment = factor(
      treatment,
      levels = c("RNO", "RIM", "RIC", "TIM", "TIC")
    ),
    lower_se = pmax(0, response - SE),
    upper_se = response + SE
  )

# Unadjusted model-based pairwise CLDs (LSD-style; no multiplicity adjustment).
# The a group is assigned to the highest estimated treatment mean.
interrow_weed_cld <- multcomp::cld(
  interrow_weed_emm,
  by = "site_year",
  adjust = "none",
  alpha = 0.05,
  Letters = letters,
  reversed = TRUE
) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  transmute(
    site_year,
    treatment,
    cld = trimws(.group)
  )

interrow_fig_data <- interrow_fig_data %>%
  left_join(interrow_weed_cld, by = c("site_year", "treatment")) %>%
  mutate(
    cld_y = response + SE + 0.05 * max(response + SE, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

# Final figure
interrow_weed_fig <- ggplot(
  interrow_fig_data,
  aes(x = treatment, y = response, fill = treatment)
) +
  geom_col(
    width = 0.7,
    color = "black",
    linewidth = 0.3
  ) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(ymin = lower_se, ymax = upper_se),
    width = 0.18,
    linewidth = 0.65
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(y = cld_y, label = cld),
    size = 4.5,
    fontface = "bold"
  ) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~ site_year,
    nrow = 1,
    labeller = labeller(
      site_year = experiment_labels
    )
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = treatment_colors,
    guide = "none"
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Management system",
    y = "Inter-row weed biomass (kg/ha)"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 16) +
  theme(
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 14
    ),
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      size = 14,
      margin = margin(t = 8)
    ),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 13),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 16),
    panel.spacing = grid::unit(1.2, "lines")
  )

interrow_weed_fig

# Save publication-quality figure
dir.create(here::here("figures"), showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
ggsave(
  filename = here::here(
    "figures",
    "interrow_weed_biomass.png"
  ),
  plot = interrow_weed_fig,
  width = 11,
  height = 6,
  dpi = 300,
  bg = "white"
)
```

# In-row weed biomass: descriptive only

Initial five-system Tweedie fits had unstable coefficients for the all-zero
RNO group in O2 East; reduced interaction models imposed constant within-method
ratios and did not reproduce some O2 West observations. Whole-plot Tweedie
averages showed underdispersion (DHARMa p = 0.046), and a log1p linear mixed
sensitivity analysis had appreciable tail departures. Because this is a
secondary outcome, no in-row significance tests are retained.

The matched-system whole-plot summary averages RIM/RIC and TIM/TIC separately,
excluding RNO because it has no matched tilled counterpart. It is descriptive
and respects termination as a whole-plot treatment.

```{r inrow-whole-plot-summary, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Whole-plot summaries for matched management systems

inrow_whole_plot <- weed_data %>%
  filter(treatment %in% c("RIM", "RIC", "TIM", "TIC")) %>%
  mutate(
    termination = factor(
      if_else(
        treatment %in% c("RIM", "RIC"),
        "Rolled",
        "Tilled"
      ),
      levels = c("Rolled", "Tilled")
    )
  ) %>%
  group_by(
    site_year,
    block_id,
    whole_plot_id,
    termination
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_inrow_biomass = mean(
      inrow_weed_biomass_kg_ha
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Confirm number of whole plots
inrow_whole_plot %>%
  count(site_year, termination)

# Descriptive summaries by termination system
inrow_whole_plot %>%
  group_by(site_year, termination) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_biomass = mean(mean_inrow_biomass),
    sd_biomass = sd(mean_inrow_biomass),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r inrow-observed-summary}
inrow_summary <- weed_data %>%
  group_by(site_year, treatment) %>%
  summarise(
    n_plots = n(),
    n_zeros = sum(inrow_weed_biomass_kg_ha == 0),
    mean_biomass = mean(inrow_weed_biomass_kg_ha),
    sd_biomass = sd(inrow_weed_biomass_kg_ha),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
show_table(inrow_summary, "Observed in-row weed biomass (kg/ha)")
```

# Combined observed weed biomass figure

The stacked treatment colors show observed arithmetic mean contributions from
inter-row (darker) and in-row (lighter). Their sum equals observed total weed
biomass. Error bars show the **observed total arithmetic mean ± SE** (four
plots per treatment/site-year). Lowercase letters summarize **unadjusted model-based pairwise Wald tests**
(Fisher LSD-style) of total weed biomass within each site-year. These letters
apply to total biomass only, not to the components; shared letters do not
establish equivalence. The SE bars are descriptive plot-to-plot variation,
not model-based uncertainty for treatment contrasts.

```{r weed-biomass-combined-final, fig.width=12, fig.height=6.5, out.width="100%", message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(emmeans)

# ----------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Treatment colors by sampling zone
# ----------------------------------------------------------

lighten_color <- function(color, amount = 0.55) {
  rgb <- grDevices::col2rgb(color) / 255
  light <- rgb + (1 - rgb) * amount

  grDevices::rgb(
    light[1, ],
    light[2, ],
    light[3, ]
  )
}

zone_colors <- c(
  setNames(
    treatment_colors,
    paste0(names(treatment_colors), "_Inter-row")
  ),
  setNames(
    vapply(
      treatment_colors,
      lighten_color,
      character(1)
    ),
    paste0(names(treatment_colors), "_In-row")
  )
)

# ----------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Observed means and SE by site-year and treatment
# ----------------------------------------------------------

weed_zone_means <- weed_data %>%
  group_by(site_year, treatment) %>%
  summarise(
    inrow = mean(inrow_weed_biomass_kg_ha),
    interrow = mean(interrow_weed_biomass_kg_ha),
    total_mean = mean(weed_biomass_kg_ha),
    total_se = sd(weed_biomass_kg_ha) / sqrt(n()),
    n_plots = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Convert zone means to long format for stacked bars
weed_zone_plot_data <- weed_zone_means %>%
  select(site_year, treatment, inrow, interrow) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(inrow, interrow),
    names_to = "zone",
    values_to = "mean_biomass"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    zone = factor(
      zone,
      levels = c("inrow", "interrow"),
      labels = c("In-row", "Inter-row")
    ),
    treatment_zone = paste(treatment, zone, sep = "_")
  )

# ----------------------------------------------------------
# 3. CLDs from the total weed biomass model
# ----------------------------------------------------------

# Reuse total_weed_emm calculated above.

# Requires multcomp and multcompView packages.
# Fisher's LSD-style CLDs use unadjusted pairwise tests within site-year.
total_weed_cld <- multcomp::cld(
  total_weed_emm,
  by = "site_year",
  adjust = "none",
  alpha = 0.05,
  Letters = letters,
  reversed = TRUE
) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  transmute(
    site_year,
    treatment,
    cld = trimws(.group)
  )

# Position letters above observed mean + SE
weed_annotations <- weed_zone_means %>%
  left_join(
    total_weed_cld,
    by = c("site_year", "treatment")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    cld_y = total_mean + total_se + 65
  )

# ----------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Combined figure
# ----------------------------------------------------------

combined_weed_model_fig <- ggplot() +

  # Observed in-row and inter-row biomass
  geom_col(
    data = weed_zone_plot_data,
    aes(
      x = treatment,
      y = mean_biomass,
      fill = treatment_zone
    ),
    width = 0.72,
    color = "black",
    linewidth = 0.3
  ) +

  # Observed total weed biomass ± SE
  geom_errorbar(
    data = weed_zone_means,
    aes(
      x = treatment,
      ymin = pmax(0, total_mean - total_se),
      ymax = total_mean + total_se
    ),
    width = 0.18,
    linewidth = 0.7,
    color = "black"
  ) +

  # Total weed biomass significance groupings
  geom_text(
    data = weed_annotations,
    aes(
      x = treatment,
      y = cld_y,
      label = cld
    ),
    size = 4.5,
    fontface = "bold"
  ) +

  facet_wrap(
    ~ site_year,
    nrow = 1,
    labeller = labeller(
      site_year = experiment_labels
    )
  ) +

  scale_fill_manual(
    values = zone_colors,
    guide = "none"
  ) +

  scale_y_continuous(
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))
  ) +

  labs(
    x = "Management system",
    y = "Total weed biomass (kg/ha)",
    caption = paste(
      "Dark shading: inter-row; light shading: in-row.",
      "Stacked bars and SE are observed totals (n = 4).",
      "Lowercase letters: unadjusted model-based total-biomass comparisons."
    )
  ) +

  theme_classic(base_size = 16) +

  theme(
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 14
    ),
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      size = 14,
      margin = margin(t = 8)
    ),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 13),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 16),
    plot.caption = element_text(
      size = 11,
      hjust = 0.5,
      margin = margin(t = 15)
    ),
    panel.spacing = grid::unit(1.2, "lines")
  )

combined_weed_model_fig

# Save figure
dir.create(here::here("figures"), showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
ggsave(
  filename = here::here(
    "figures",
    "weed_biomass_combined_final.png"
  ),
  plot = combined_weed_model_fig,
  width = 12,
  height = 6.5,
  dpi = 300,
  bg = "white"
)
```

# Interpretation and limitations

Across experiments, total weed biomass and its spatial distribution varied
substantially among management systems and site-years. In 2023, TIC showed very
little inter-row weed biomass but considerable in-row biomass; the separate
inter-row model provides tests specific to the directly managed zone. In
O2 West 2024, the unadjusted total-biomass CLDs distinguished TIC (b)
from RNO, RIC, and TIM (a), while RIM (ab) was not distinguishable from
either group. The planned RIC versus TIC total-biomass contrast also passed
the within-site-year Holm adjustment (p approximately 0.047). These results
should be interpreted cautiously because the unadjusted CLDs do not control
familywise error and asymptotic Wald tests may be poorly calibrated with only
four blocks per site-year. Some inter-row contrasts were also significant,
but those address a separate response.

Cereal rye biomass collected before termination and from the weed quadrats,
and subsequent soybean yield analyses, will be considered later for mechanistic
and outcome relationships. Those variables are intentionally not introduced
into these baseline treatment-effect models.

Before reporting, verify 2023 implementation details, processed-data units,
randomization, and the chosen inference families. Total and inter-row CLDs
reflect unadjusted model-based pairwise Wald comparisons (unprotected Fisher
LSD-style). Holm-adjusted p-values for selected contrasts are reported
separately; their confidence intervals use Bonferroni adjustment. Near-zero
random-effect variance estimates and four blocks per site-year limit confidence
in asymptotic, especially borderline cross-termination, inference. The sign-
flip enumeration is an assumption-dependent sensitivity check, not confirmed
as an exact randomization test.
